mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) over three consecutive months indicates strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of corporate earnings growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods following a sustained increase in RSAFS over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic activity slows and consumer spending decreases.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a UNRATE increase > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two consecutive months signals a supply-side contraction, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are negatively impacted.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods following a decrease in INDPRO by more than 1% over two months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods following a HOUST increase > 5% over three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increase > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances following the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 over a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200,000 and UNRATE decrease > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods following the trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals strong economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are positively impacted.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods following a sustained increase in GDPC1 over two quarters.
